newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds higher, spreads firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds higher, spreads firm.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds rose in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries at midday, following a dose of bond-friendly manufacturing data, and spreads held firm, traders said.
Junk bonds were also firmer in lackluster trade, meanwhile. New issues traded higher but without the gusto seen last week, traders said.
In the high-grades market, issuance was trading near original levels, traders said, reflecting both strong technicals and quiet trade.

Conagra Inc's $400 million Baa1/BBB-rated 30-year senior notes, putable in the tenth year, were little changed at 50 to 51 basis points bid. Smith Barney Inc priced the notes on Monday to yield 50 basis points over Treasuries.

Elsewhere, Bankers Trust New York's $250 million A2/single-A-rated five-year senior notes widened slightly to a 44 bid, 42 offer market at mid-session compared with an issue spread of 40 basis points.

Traders said the wider market was not an indication of weakness, however, and the bulk of bank and finance paper was largely unchanged. Most bank and finance paper has been priced very aggressively in the past month, they added.

In the governments market, U.S. Treasuries were lifted at mid-morning after the National Association of Purchasing Managers said its index of manufacturing activity fell to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August.
The 30-year Treasury bond was quoted up 15/32 to yield 6.89 percent at 1127 EDT/1527 GMT.
Turning to high-yielders, traders said fresh paper continued to trade up, though not as aggresively as last week.

RSL Communications's 10-year notes, priced yesterday at par to yield 12.25 were quoted midday at 100-5/8 bid, 101-1/4 offer. Boyd Gaming Corp, priced late on Monday at 99.597, climbed to 99.725 in thin trade.
Elsewhere, news that Echostar is negotiating with phone giant Sprint for an alliance helped Echostar trade higher. Echostar was quoted up 2 points at 70 to 71-1/2 bid and 80 to 81 offer.
Sprint Spectrum's zeros were little changed at 58-1/2 bid, 58-5/8 offer, a trader said.
Other telecoms posted mixed performances at midday.
Adelphia, one of yesterday's key losers, continued to trade lower, with the 12-1/2 percent debt quoted at 104-5/8 bid, 105 offer.
But Mobilmedia Communications, whose poor earnings report sapped prices on Monday, staged a rebound. Mobilmedia's coupons were quoted at 81 bid, 81-1/2 offer, up from 78 bid, 80 offer on Monday.
